items.name: Senso-ji Temple (Asakusa)
items.kicker: Tokyo's oldest temple, and a food street in front of it
items.body: Free to enter, main hall open 6:00 AM–5:00 PM (6:30 AM Oct–Mar). Nakamise-dori, the approach street, is itself a food stop — senbei, menchi-katsu, age-manju — so this pairs naturally with a food-crawl morning rather than needing a separate stop.

items.name: Meiji Jingu
items.kicker: A forested shrine between Harajuku and Yoyogi Park
items.body:
Free to enter the grounds; gate hours track sunrise/sunset (roughly 5:00 AM–6:40 PM depending on season). Weekday early morning, right at gate opening, is the genuinely quiet window — multiple recent accounts describe the paths as nearly empty before the tour groups arrive, with crowds building steadily through the day.

Adjoins Harajuku/Omotesando, so it pairs well with a street-food or café stop.

items.name: teamLab Planets (Toyosu)
items.kicker: Immersive digital-art museum, walk barefoot through water
items.body: ≈¥3,800 weekday / ¥4,200 weekend adult, timed entry. ⚠ Closes for maintenance roughly monthly on irregular dates — check teamlab.art's live calendar before booking. Toyosu is also where the fish market wholesale trade relocated (see below), so a sushi breakfast pairs naturally with this stop.

items.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
items.kicker: A large formal garden minutes from Shinjuku's density
items.body: Oct 1–Mar 14 hours: 9:00 AM–4:30 PM, last entry 4:00 PM. Adults ¥500. Closed every Monday — Mon Oct 19 falls inside this trip and isn't a substitute holiday, so plan the garden for one of the other four days.

items.name: Tokyo Tower
items.kicker: The cheaper, less-crowded skyline view — near Roppongi/Azabudai's dining scene
items.body: Main Deck from ¥1,500, opens 9:00 AM. Multiple comparisons note Tokyo Tower gives a more grounded skyline view than Skytree's 450m deck, which shrinks landmarks to miniatures — a reasonable trade for a group that isn't prioritizing sightseeing.

items.name: Yanaka Ginza
items.kicker: An old-Tokyo shopping street that IS the sightseeing — eat your way down it
items.body: A ~170m street of 60–70 independent shops, 5 minutes from Nippori Station. Street-food staples: menchi-katsu (fried minced-meat cutlet), grilled seafood skewers. The best fit in this guide's Sights section for a food-priority trip — there's no separate "sight" here, the street food is the point.

items.claim: Go to Tsukiji to see the famous tuna auction.
items.correction: The wholesale market and its tuna auction moved to Toyosu in October 2018. Tsukiji's outer market (food stalls and restaurants) is still open and worth visiting — but the auction itself is only viewable at Toyosu now.

The original Odaiba location permanently closed in August 2022. teamLab Borderless reopened at Azabudai Hills in February 2024 — any guide still pointing to Odaiba is sending you to a closed building.

items.claim: Meiji Jingu's forest is an ancient, natural woodland.
items.correction: It's a deliberately engineered forest, planted from barren grassland starting in 1915 and designed to read as ancient after roughly 150 years — impressive, but not what most guides imply.
